title: The Office - Sending A Quote Via Email
audio: mp3/315. The Office - Sending A Quote Via Email.mp3

segments.en: Hello everyone and welcome to EnglishPod.
segments.zh: 大家好，欢迎来到 EnglishPod。

segments.en: My name is Marco.
segments.zh: 我叫 Marco。

segments.en: My name is Kathryn and we have an unusual lesson for you today.
segments.zh: 我的名字是凯瑟琳，我们今天给你们准备了一节不同寻常的课。

segments.en: It's more about writing than about speaking.
segments.zh: 更多的是写作而不是说话。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: Well, many times we have to write emails and if we're working in a sales environment, we may need to write an email to a potential client.
segments.zh: 好吧，很多时候我们必须写电子邮件，如果我们在销售环境中工作，我们可能需要给潜在客户写一封电子邮件。

segments.en: Alright, so we're going to learn what is appropriate and what is not in today's lesson.
segments.zh: 好吧，所以我们将学习今天课程中什么是合适的，什么是不合适的。

segments.en: Let's take a listen to our dialogue.
segments.zh: 我们来听听对话。

segments.en: Melanie, can you help me with something?
segments.zh: 梅兰妮，你能帮我做点什么吗？

segments.en: We need to finalize the account with the Mexican embassy and I need some advice on phrasing this letter correctly in English.
segments.zh: 我们得把墨西哥大使馆这笔业务敲定，我想请你帮忙看看这封英文信怎么措辞才合适。

segments.en: Sure Tracy, let me just get my laptop.
segments.zh: 当然，特蕾西，让我拿我的笔记本电脑。

segments.en: Right, all set.
segments.zh: 好了，准备好了。

segments.en: Ok, so, to whom it may concern, I am writing…
segments.zh: 那么，先写：“敬启者：我写此信……”

segments.en: Um, Tracy, I think that's a little too formal.
segments.zh: 嗯，特蕾西，我认为这有点太正式了。

segments.en: I know you want to be polite, but you've already made contact with them, so in English, you can be a bit more relaxed in the opening.
segments.zh: 我知道你要有礼貌，但你已经和他们取得了联系，所以用英语，你可以在开场白中放松一点。

segments.en: Ok, more relaxed.
segments.zh: 好吧，更轻松。

segments.en: Got it.
segments.zh: 明白了。

segments.en: Hey Sally, what's up?
segments.zh: 嘿，莎莉，怎么了？

segments.en: It's Tracy here, just…
segments.zh: 这里是特蕾西，只是……

segments.en: Ok, Tracy, now it's too relaxed.
segments.zh: 好吧，特蕾西，现在太放松了。

segments.en: You've still got to show some respect.
segments.zh: 你还是要表现出一些尊重。

segments.en: How about starting with Dear Miss Cooper, I'm writing to confirm…
segments.zh: 以“亲爱的库珀小姐，我写信是为了确认……”开头怎么样？

segments.en: Great, ok.
segments.zh: 太好了，好的。

segments.en: Dear Miss Cooper, I'm writing to confirm the final quotation for the full-page back cover color advertisement you requested for the spring issue of Viola Magazine.
segments.zh: 亲爱的库珀小姐，我写信是为了确认您在 Viola 杂志的春季刊上要求的整页封底彩色广告的最终报价。

segments.en: That's great.
segments.zh: 太好了。

segments.en: The final costing, including advert design and production, comes to 45,600 RMB.
segments.zh: 包含广告设计和制作在内，最终总费用为四万五千六百元人民币。

segments.en: We want payment 10 working days before publication, or we will cancel the ad.
segments.zh: 我们希望在发布前 10 个工作日付款，否则我们将取消广告。

segments.en: Thanks for…
segments.zh: 感谢…

segments.en: Whoa, ok, back up a second Tracy.
segments.zh: 等等，特蕾西，先回头看看这一句。

segments.en: That's too direct.
segments.zh: 这太直接了。

segments.en: Can I suggest you say, please note that the final payment is due two working weeks before publication.
segments.zh: 我可以建议您说，请注意，最终付款应在发布前两周到期。

segments.en: You don't want to offend her.
segments.zh: 你不想冒犯她。

segments.en: Oops, ok, you're right.
segments.zh: 哎呀，好吧，你是对的。

segments.en: Then I can just end with, all the best, Tracy.
segments.zh: 然后我就可以用“一切顺利，特蕾西”来结尾。

segments.en: Hmm, maybe I'd play it safe and just finish with, yours sincerely.
segments.zh: 我觉得稳妥一点，还是用“此致敬礼”结尾吧。

segments.en: That's more professional.
segments.zh: 这样更专业。

segments.en: Oh, Melanie, you're a lifesaver.
segments.zh: 哦，梅兰妮，你真是救星。

segments.en: Thank you.
segments.zh: 谢谢。

segments.en: Alright, we're back, so now let's take a look at some of that vocab we heard on Language Takeaway.
segments.zh: 好吧，我们回来了，现在让我们来看看我们在语言要点中听到的一些词汇。

segments.en: Language Takeaway.
segments.zh: 语言要点。

segments.en: We have some wonderful adjectives today.
segments.zh: 我们今天有一些很棒的形容词。

segments.en: The first one that I wanted to discuss, Marco, is formal.
segments.zh: 我想讨论的第一个，Marco，是正式的。

segments.en: Formal, that's right.
segments.zh: 正规的，没错。

segments.en: We want to be a little bit more formal when we're writing someone we don't really know too much.
segments.zh: 当我们写一个我们不太了解的人时，我们希望变得更正式一点。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: But be careful because sometimes you can be too formal.
segments.zh: 但要小心，因为有时你可能太正式了。

segments.en: So what exactly does formal mean?
segments.zh: 那么正式是什么意思呢？

segments.en: So if you write a formal email, it's very proper, very respectful.
segments.zh: 所以如果你写一封正式的电子邮件，它是非常恰当的，非常尊重的。

segments.en: So proper in the way that you wouldn't use colloquial terms or phrasal verbs that you would use with your friends.
segments.zh: 也就是说，你不会像跟朋友聊天那样使用口语化的说法或短语动词。

segments.en: No, a good example is writing to a lawyer or a judge.
segments.zh: 不，一个很好的例子是写信给律师或法官。

segments.en: You want to use formal language.
segments.zh: 你想使用正式的语言。

segments.en: Even with a teacher, you might use more formal language.
segments.zh: 即使是对老师，你也可能用更正式的语言。

segments.en: But with a friend, you don't have to.
segments.zh: 但和朋友就不必这样。

segments.en: That's something else.
segments.zh: 那又是另一回事。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So when you're writing something that's formal, it's important to be polite as well.
segments.zh: 所以当你写一些正式的东西时，礼貌也很重要。

segments.en: Now what is polite?
segments.zh: 现在什么是礼貌？

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: So you want to be formal, you want to be serious, and you want to be polite.
segments.zh: 所以你想正式，你想认真，你想礼貌。

segments.en: You want to show respect.
segments.zh: 你想表达尊重。

segments.en: You want to be nice, basically.
segments.zh: 你想变得友善，基本上。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: And so people can often be described as polite.
segments.zh: 所以人们通常可以被描述为礼貌。

segments.en: He's very polite or she's not polite at all.
segments.zh: 他很有礼貌，或者她一点也不礼貌。

segments.en: And when I was a little kid, my mom used to say, it's very important to be polite.
segments.zh: 当我还是个小孩的时候，我妈妈常说，礼貌很重要。

segments.en: You say thank you and you're welcome when you're talking to other people.
segments.zh: 和别人交谈时，你会说“谢谢”和“不客气”。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: And that's one way of being polite.
segments.zh: 这是礼貌的一种方式。

segments.en: Now also when we are describing the way that you speak to someone or the way that you write, you can be very direct.
segments.zh: 现在，当我们描述您与某人交谈的方式或写作方式时，您可以非常直接。

segments.en: Now being direct means that you say exactly what you want or exactly what you're thinking.
segments.zh: 现在直接意味着你准确地说出你想要的或你在想什么。

segments.en: Okay, so maybe if we're talking to this company, you say, hi, I want this.
segments.zh: 好吧，也许如果我们正在与这家公司交谈，你会说，嗨，我想要这个。

segments.en: I will pay this much.
segments.zh: 我会付这么多。

segments.en: Thank you.
segments.zh: 谢谢。

segments.en: Bye.
segments.zh: 再见。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: That's maybe too direct.
segments.zh: 这可能太直接了。

segments.en: You need to be a little less direct and say nice things in an email.
segments.zh: 你需要稍微委婉一点，在邮件里说些客气话。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So maybe you want to say to someone that you don't really like the clothes they're wearing, right?
segments.zh: 所以也许你想对某人说你不喜欢他们穿的衣服，对吧？

segments.en: You say, hey, do you like my new shirt?
segments.zh: 你说，嘿，你喜欢我的新衬衫吗？

segments.en: And if you're very direct, you would say, no, I think it's very ugly.
segments.zh: 如果你很直接，你会说，不，我认为这很丑陋。

segments.en: I hate it.
segments.zh: 我讨厌它。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: That's too direct.
segments.zh: 这太直接了。

segments.en: So maybe you would say, I don't really think it suits you very well.
segments.zh: 所以也许你会说，我真的不认为它很适合你。

segments.en: Or I think a different color would be better on you.
segments.zh: 或者我认为不同的颜色对你会更好。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So that's being a little bit less direct.
segments.zh: 所以这有点不那么直接了。

segments.en: Now obviously, if you're too direct with someone, you may offend that person.
segments.zh: 现在很明显，如果你对某人太直接，你可能会冒犯那个人。

segments.en: Alright, to offend is a verb and to offend someone means to say something that makes them unhappy or upset or even angry.
segments.zh: 好吧，冒犯是一个动词，冒犯某人意味着说一些让他们不开心、不高兴甚至生气的话。

segments.en: So going back to the same example of the shirt, if you say, I think that shirt is very ugly, that person might be offended.
segments.zh: 所以回到同样的衬衫例子，如果你说，我认为那件衬衫很丑，那个人可能会被冒犯。

segments.en: Gosh.
segments.zh: 天哪。

segments.en: Or maybe if you say, I think people with brown hair are so ugly and there's someone next to me with brown hair, they say, oh, I'm offended.
segments.zh: 或者如果你说，我认为棕色头发的人是如此丑陋，我旁边有人长着棕色头发，他们说，哦，我被冒犯了。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: I'm not ugly, but I have brown hair.
segments.zh: 我不丑，但我有一头棕色的头发。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: Okay, so you don't want to offend anyone by being too direct or you don't want to have anyone feel offended.
segments.zh: 好吧，所以你不想因为太直接而冒犯别人，也不希望有人感到被冒犯。

segments.en: Now for our last phrase here on Language Takeaway, we have towards the end of the dialogue, Tracy thanks Melanie by saying, you are a lifesaver.
segments.zh: 现在来看语言要点的最后一个短语。在对话结尾，特蕾西感谢梅兰妮时说：“你真是救星。”

segments.en: Thank you.
segments.zh: 谢谢。

segments.en: Okay, so don't be confused.
segments.zh: 好吧，所以不要混淆。

segments.en: There is also a candy called lifesavers and she's not calling her a candy.
segments.zh: 还有一种叫 Lifesavers 的糖果，她不是把她叫成糖果。

segments.en: She's saying, wow, thank you.
segments.zh: 她说，哇，谢谢。

segments.en: You really helped me.
segments.zh: 你真的帮助了我。

segments.en: So when someone helps you a lot, you can call them a lifesaver.
segments.zh: 因此，当有人帮了你很多忙时，你可以叫他救星。

segments.en: Marco, what exactly is the object, the lifesaver?
segments.zh: 马可，那个叫 lifesaver 的实物到底是什么？

segments.en: If you've ever been on a boat, you see this big orange circle that is used to throw into the water to help someone to prevent them from drowning.
segments.zh: 如果你曾经在船上，你会看到这个橙色的大圆圈，它被用来扔进水里，以帮助别人防止他们溺水。

segments.en: That is called a lifesaver.
segments.zh: 这就叫救生圈。

segments.en: Okay, so I'm drowning.
segments.zh: 好吧，所以我溺水了。

segments.en: I'm having a hard time writing this email.
segments.zh: 我很难写这封电子邮件。

segments.en: I do not know what to say.
segments.zh: 我不知道该说什么。

segments.en: Marco, you come and help me.
segments.zh: 马可，你来帮助我。

segments.en: I can say, oh wow, thank you so much.
segments.zh: 我可以说，哦，哇，非常感谢。

segments.en: You're a lifesaver.
segments.zh: 你真是救星。

segments.en: That's exactly right.
segments.zh: 完全正确。

segments.en: All right, so we've taken a look at five key words there.
segments.zh: 好吧，所以我们在那里看了五个关键词。

segments.en: Why don't we take a listen to our dialogue again and we'll be back with Fluency Builder.
segments.zh: 我们为什么不再听听对话，我们稍后会带着流利表达回来。

segments.en: Melanie, can you help me with something?
segments.zh: 梅兰妮，你能帮我做点什么吗？

segments.en: We need to finalize the account with the Mexican embassy and I need some advice on phrasing this letter correctly in English.
segments.zh: 我们得把墨西哥大使馆这笔业务敲定，我想请你帮忙看看这封英文信怎么措辞才合适。

segments.en: Sure Tracy, let me just get my laptop.
segments.zh: 当然，特蕾西，让我拿我的笔记本电脑。

segments.en: Right, all set.
segments.zh: 好了，都准备好了。

segments.en: Okay, so to whom it may concern, I am writing...
segments.zh: 好，那么，敬启者：我写此信……

segments.en: Tracy, I think that's a little too formal.
segments.zh: 特蕾西，我认为这有点太正式了。

segments.en: I know you want to be polite, but you've already made contact with them, so in English, you can be a bit more relaxed in the opening.
segments.zh: 我知道你要有礼貌，但你已经和他们取得了联系，所以用英语，你可以在开场白中放松一点。

segments.en: Okay, more relaxed.
segments.zh: 好吧，更轻松。

segments.en: Got it.
segments.zh: 明白了。

segments.en: Hey Sally, what's up?
segments.zh: 嘿，莎莉，怎么了？

segments.en: It's Tracy here, just...
segments.zh: 这里是特蕾西，只是...

segments.en: Okay Tracy, now it's too relaxed.
segments.zh: 好吧，特蕾西，现在太放松了。

segments.en: You've still got to show some respect.
segments.zh: 你还是要表现出一些尊重。

segments.en: How about starting with, dear Miss Cooper, I'm writing to confirm...
segments.zh: 以“亲爱的库珀小姐，我写信是为了确认……”开头怎么样？

segments.en: Great, okay.
segments.zh: 太好了，好的。

segments.en: Dear Miss Cooper, I'm writing to confirm the final quotation for the full-page back cover color advertisement you requested for the spring issue of Viola Magazine.
segments.zh: 亲爱的库珀小姐，我写信是为了确认您在 Viola 杂志的春季刊上要求的整页封底彩色广告的最终报价。

segments.en: That's great.
segments.zh: 太好了。

segments.en: The final costing, including advert design and production, comes to 45,600 RMB.
segments.zh: 包含广告设计和制作在内，最终总费用为四万五千六百元人民币。

segments.en: We want payment 10 working days before publication, or we will cancel the ad.
segments.zh: 我们希望在发布前 10 个工作日付款，否则我们将取消广告。

segments.en: Thanks for...
segments.zh: 感谢...

segments.en: Whoa, okay, back up a second Tracy.
segments.zh: 哇，等一下，特蕾西，退回去一点。

segments.en: That's too direct.
segments.zh: 这太直接了。

segments.en: Can I suggest you say, please note that the final payment is due two working weeks before publication.
segments.zh: 我可以建议您说，请注意，最终付款应在发布前两周到期。

segments.en: You don't want to offend her.
segments.zh: 你不想冒犯她。

segments.en: Oops, okay, you're right.
segments.zh: 哎呀，好吧，你是对的。

segments.en: Then I can just end with, all the best, Tracy.
segments.zh: 然后我就可以用“一切顺利，特蕾西”来结尾。

segments.en: Maybe I'd play it safe and just finish with, yours sincerely.
segments.zh: 也许我会稳妥一点，直接用“此致敬礼”结尾。

segments.en: That's more professional.
segments.zh: 这样更专业。

segments.en: Oh, Melanie, you're a lifesaver.
segments.zh: 哦，梅兰妮，你真是救星。

segments.en: Thank you.
segments.zh: 谢谢。

segments.en: So today in Fluency Builder we have a number of phrases you can use when you're writing an email.
segments.zh: 因此，今天在流利表达中，我们有许多短语可以在您写电子邮件时使用。

segments.en: Some of them are very polite and formal.
segments.zh: 其中一些非常有礼貌、很正式。

segments.en: Some of them are very informal or casual.
segments.zh: 其中一些非常非正式或随意。

segments.en: Now this first phrase, Marco, is very, very formal, right?
segments.zh: 现在第一个短语，马可，非常非常正式，对吧？

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: You start the letter by stating, to whom it may concern.
segments.zh: 信的开头你就写：“敬启者”。

segments.en: All right, to whom it may concern.
segments.zh: 好，“敬启者”。

segments.en: Remember that M there.
segments.zh: 记住那里的M。

segments.en: This is a very formal phrase and we're going to take it as a phrase.
segments.zh: 这是一个非常正式的短语，我们将把它当作一个短语。

segments.en: This is how you begin a formal letter.
segments.zh: 这就是你开始正式信的方式。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: Usually you start this letter if it's directed to maybe a company or someone not specific.
segments.zh: 通常，如果这封信是寄给某家公司或不特定的人，你才会这样开头。

segments.en: You don't know that person's name and you're just saying, you know, whoever's reading this letter, whoever it concerns.
segments.zh: 你不知道那个人的名字，你只是在说，你知道，谁在读这封信，不管它涉及谁。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: Well, I could say, dear Marco, but in this case, maybe I don't know who the name of the person I am writing this email to.
segments.zh: 好吧，我可以说 dear Marco，但在这种情况下，也许我并不知道我写这封邮件的人叫什么名字。

segments.en: It's a big company.
segments.zh: 这是一家大公司。

segments.en: There are many people.
segments.zh: 有很多人。

segments.en: So if you don't know who you're writing to in a company or in an organization, you say, to whom it may concern.
segments.zh: 因此，如果你在公司或机构里不知道该写给谁，你就写“敬启者”。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: Now we started very formal.
segments.zh: 现在我们开始非常正式。

segments.en: Melanie said, I think it's a little bit too formal.
segments.zh: 梅兰妮说，我觉得有点太正式了。

segments.en: Maybe we should be more relaxed.
segments.zh: 也许我们应该更放松。

segments.en: So Tracy says, okay, got it.
segments.zh: 所以特蕾西说，好吧，明白了。

segments.en: So how about, hey Sally, what's up?
segments.zh: 那么，嘿，莎莉，怎么了？

segments.en: What's up?
segments.zh: 最近怎么样？

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So what's up is the kind of thing I say with my friends, you know, hey Marco, what's up?
segments.zh: 那么我和朋友们说的那种话，你知道，嘿，马可，怎么了？

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: But I would never say this in a formal situation with a boss or with a, you know, an employer or with a, um, in more serious situation.
segments.zh: 但我永远不会在正式场合这么说，比如和老板、和雇主，嗯，或者更严肃的场合。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: Especially if you're writing a, an email to a client, you don't really want to say what's up.
segments.zh: 特别是给客户写邮件时，你真的不该说 what's up。

segments.en: No, never.
segments.zh: 不，从来没有。

segments.en: So remember this is spoken English with your friends, but not something you would write.
segments.zh: 所以记住，这是和朋友之间的口语，不是你会写进信里的东西。

segments.en: Um, so the key here is that you have to show some respect.
segments.zh: 嗯，所以这里的关键是你必须表现出一些尊重。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So that's another great phrase, you show some respect.
segments.zh: 所以这是另一个很棒的短语，你表现出一些尊重。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So the key here is that this is, um, the verb is to show, right?
segments.zh: 所以这里的关键是，嗯，动词是要展示，对吧？

segments.en: Not to give.
segments.zh: 不给。

segments.en: Um, you want to show respect to someone.
segments.zh: 嗯，你想对某人表示尊重。

segments.en: Well, how do you show respect?
segments.zh: 那么，你如何表达尊重？

segments.en: Well, the way that you act, your behaviors.
segments.zh: 好吧，你的行为方式，你的行为。

segments.en: So if I'm polite and I say, you know, Mr. and Miss and thank you and please, these are ways to show respect.
segments.zh: 所以如果我有礼貌，会说“先生”“小姐”，还有“谢谢”“请”，这些都是表达尊重的方式。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So that's the way that you are being respectful.
segments.zh: 所以这就是你尊重的方式。

segments.en: You are showing respect by being very polite.
segments.zh: 你非常有礼貌地表现出尊重。

segments.en: For example, in Japan, it is common to take your shoes off when you go to a friend's home, their house in order to show respect to them.
segments.zh: 例如，在日本，去朋友家时脱鞋以表达对他们的尊重是很常见的。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: Very good.
segments.zh: 很好。

segments.en: Now, as we continue writing the letter towards the end, we wanted to play it safe and just write your sincerely to close the letter off.
segments.zh: 现在，信写到结尾时，我们想稳妥一点，就用 yours sincerely 来收尾。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So this phrase, play it safe.
segments.zh: 所以这个短语，play it safe（稳妥行事）。

segments.en: What does this mean?
segments.zh: 这是什么意思？

segments.en: When we're talking about making a decision or taking a risk, we want to play it safe.
segments.zh: 当我们谈论做决定或冒风险时，我们会想稳妥行事。

segments.en: We want to use the less risky option.
segments.zh: 我们希望使用风险较小的选项。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So the key here is that the verb is to play.
segments.zh: 所以这里的关键是，动词是 play。

segments.en: Play it safe.
segments.zh: 稳妥行事。

segments.en: This means that, yeah, there's maybe a risky option and a safe option and it's better to take the safe option.
segments.zh: 这意味着，是的，可能有一个冒险的选项和一个安全的选项，最好选择安全的选项。

segments.en: Play it safe.
segments.zh: 稳妥行事。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So that's the way that you would use this phrase to play it safe, to make a decision that doesn't have too much risk or that you know that will work very well.
segments.zh: 所以这就是 play it safe 的用法——做一个没有太大风险、或者你确信会很顺利的决定。

segments.en: And to close things off, another option to end the letter, we could say, all the best.
segments.zh: 最后，结束这封信的另一个选择，我们可以写 all the best。

segments.en: All the best, Tracy.
segments.zh: 一切顺利，特蕾西。

segments.en: All the best, Tracy.
segments.zh: 一切顺利，特蕾西。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So this is a way to end a letter.
segments.zh: 所以这是结束信的一种方式。

segments.en: You can say sincerely or best, but it's a very nice way to end if you just say all the best and then you say, you know, after that you have a comma and then you sign your name.
segments.zh: 你可以写 sincerely 或 best，但直接写 all the best 收尾也很好——后面加个逗号，然后签上你的名字。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: Let's listen to our dialogue one last time and we'll be back to talk a little bit more.
segments.zh: 让我们最后一次听我们的对话，我们会回来多说一点。

segments.en: Melanie, can you help me with something?
segments.zh: 梅兰妮，你能帮我做点什么吗？

segments.en: We need to finalize the account with the Mexican embassy and I need some advice on phrasing this letter correctly in English.
segments.zh: 我们得把墨西哥大使馆这笔业务敲定，我想请你帮忙看看这封英文信怎么措辞才合适。

segments.en: Sure, Tracy.
segments.zh: 当然，特蕾西。

segments.en: Let me just get my laptop.
segments.zh: 让我拿我的笔记本电脑。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: All set.
segments.zh: 都准备好了。

segments.en: Okay, so to whom it may concern, I am writing...
segments.zh: 好，那么，敬启者：我写此信……

segments.en: Tracy, I think that's a little too formal.
segments.zh: 特蕾西，我认为这有点太正式了。

segments.en: I know you want to be polite, but you've already made contact with them.
segments.zh: 我知道你要有礼貌，但你已经和他们取得了联系。

segments.en: So in English, you can be a bit more relaxed in the opening.
segments.zh: 所以在英语中，你可以在开口处放松一点。

segments.en: Okay, more relaxed.
segments.zh: 好吧，更轻松。

segments.en: Got it.
segments.zh: 明白了。

segments.en: Hey, Sally, what's up?
segments.zh: 嘿，莎莉，怎么了？

segments.en: It's Tracy here.
segments.zh: 这是特蕾西。

segments.en: Just...
segments.zh: 只是...

segments.en: Okay, Tracy.
segments.zh: 好吧，特蕾西。

segments.en: Now it's too relaxed.
segments.zh: 现在它太放松了。

segments.en: You've still got to show some respect.
segments.zh: 你还是要表现出一些尊重。

segments.en: How about starting with Dear Miss Cooper, I'm writing to confirm...
segments.zh: 以“亲爱的库珀小姐，我写信确认……”开头怎么样？

segments.en: Great.
segments.zh: 太好了。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: Dear Miss Cooper, I'm writing to confirm the final quotation for the full page back cover color advertisement you requested for the spring issue of Viola Magazine.
segments.zh: 亲爱的库珀小姐，我写信是为了确认您在 Viola 杂志的春季刊上要求的整页封底彩色广告的最终报价。

segments.en: That's great.
segments.zh: 太好了。

segments.en: The final costing, including advert design and production, comes to 45,600 RMB.
segments.zh: 包含广告设计和制作在内，最终总费用为四万五千六百元人民币。

segments.en: We want payment 10 working days before publication, or we will cancel the ad.
segments.zh: 我们希望在发布前 10 个工作日付款，否则我们将取消广告。

segments.en: Thanks for...
segments.zh: 感谢...

segments.en: Whoa.
segments.zh: 哇。

segments.en: Okay, back up a second, Tracy.
segments.zh: 好，等一下，特蕾西，退回去一点。

segments.en: That's too direct.
segments.zh: 这太直接了。

segments.en: Can I suggest you say, please note that the final payment is due two working weeks before publication.
segments.zh: 我可以建议您说，请注意，最终付款应在发布前两周到期。

segments.en: You don't want to offend her.
segments.zh: 你不想冒犯她。

segments.en: Oops.
segments.zh: 哎呀。

segments.en: Okay, you're right.
segments.zh: 好吧，你是对的。

segments.en: Then I can just end with, all the best, Tracy.
segments.zh: 然后我就可以用“一切顺利，特蕾西”来结尾。

segments.en: Maybe I'd play it safe and just finish with, yours sincerely.
segments.zh: 也许我会稳妥一点，直接用“此致敬礼”结尾。

segments.en: That's more professional.
segments.zh: 这样更专业。

segments.en: Oh, Melanie, you're a lifesaver.
segments.zh: 哦，梅兰妮，你真是救星。

segments.en: Thank you.
segments.zh: 谢谢。

segments.en: So talking about ending formal emails or emails that you're writing to clients, colleagues, we can say sincerely, and your name, sincerely, Marco.
segments.zh: 说到给客户、同事写的正式邮件怎么结尾，我们可以写 sincerely，再加上你的名字，比如 sincerely, Marco。

segments.en: You can say, all the best, best regards.
segments.zh: 你可以说 all the best、best regards。

segments.en: Now I've noticed that some people who aren't native English speakers, sometimes they will close a letter, maybe even a formal letter, saying, yours truly, Marco, for example.
segments.zh: 我注意到有些非英语母语的人，有时会在信末——哪怕是一封正式信件——写 yours truly，比如 yours truly, Marco。

segments.en: Is that really appropriate for a business setting or a client?
segments.zh: 这真的适合商业环境或客户吗？

segments.en: I would not use yours truly.
segments.zh: 我不会用 yours truly。

segments.en: Maybe if you're trying to build a relationship with your client and you're very honest, but it seems to me to be very personal.
segments.zh: 也许如果你想和你的客户建立关系，而且你很诚实，但在我看来，这很私人。

segments.en: Very romantic.
segments.zh: 真浪漫。

segments.en: Yes, yours truly.
segments.zh: 对，yours truly。

segments.en: So I would say in that case, use sincerely or kind regards, or regards, which are a little bit more professional and less emotional.
segments.zh: 所以在那种情况下，我会说用 sincerely、kind regards 或 regards，这些更专业、也没那么情绪化。

segments.en: If you want to have a romantic letter, you can say, all my love or love or yours truly or yours faithfully.
segments.zh: 如果你想写一封浪漫的信，可以写 all my love、love，或者 yours truly、yours faithfully。

segments.en: This is a very important topic, I think, because many times in school we do learn how to write letters, but usually they are more personal letters.
segments.zh: 我认为这是一个非常重要的话题，因为在学校很多时候我们确实会学习如何写信，但通常它们更是个人信件。

segments.en: And so we memorize that usually at the end of the email or the end of the letter, you say yours, Marco, or yours truly, Marco.
segments.zh: 所以我们记牢了：邮件或信件的末尾要写 yours, Marco 或 yours truly, Marco。

segments.en: And although it is correct, it's not really appropriate for a professional setting.
segments.zh: 虽然它是正确的，但它并不适合专业环境。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: Just a reminder, if you're signing off your email or your letter and you're at an office, you're in your company, you want to say best or best regards or some of the things that we talked about here today.
segments.zh: 提醒一下，如果你是在办公室、在公司里给邮件或信件署名，你想写 best、best regards，或者我们今天聊到的其他说法。

segments.en: Very good.
segments.zh: 很好。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So if you have any questions or any other doubts, you can always find us at EnglishPod.com and we'll see you guys there.
segments.zh: 因此，如果您有任何问题或任何其他疑问，您可以随时在 Englishpod.com 找到我们，我们会在那里见到你们。

segments.en: Bye.
segments.zh: 再见。

segments.en: Bye-bye.
segments.zh: 拜拜。
